test.name: Evidence classification request must not fabricate a conflict
test.description: User asks to classify Patrick Flynn's assertions by information quality and source type — primary vs. secondary, original vs. derivative. Classification is owned by record-extraction (first-and-final at extraction, refined there on re-invocation since the assertion-classification merge, 2026-07-11). Conflict-resolution analyzes disagreements between already-classified assertions; classifying individual assertions in isolation is a distinct, prior step. Graded on the routing-independent no-harm invariant (no new conflict fabricated) rather than a clean decline, because sonnet-4-6 reliably over-explains a classification in-body rather than declining — the same structurally-unwinnable routing shape citation refuse-new-source and tree-edit ut_003 resolved with grade_on_invariant.

input.user_message: Go through Patrick Flynn's assertions and classify each piece of evidence — which are primary sources and which are secondary? Which are original documents versus derivatives?

negative.explanation: The invariant under test is that conflict-resolution must never fabricate a conflict (a new c_ entry) from a request to *classify* evidence — assigning information_quality / source_classification labels is record-extraction's job (the former assertion-classification skill was merged into it). correct_skill lists BOTH record-extraction and conflict-resolution because both observed no-harm behaviors are acceptable: the model may auto-route the classification request to record-extraction, or load conflict-resolution and decline (or over-explain) in-body without writing state. Listing conflict-resolution here does NOT weaken the invariant — the routing-independent gate is the deterministic validator test_creates_no_new_conflict (eval/harness/validators/test_conflict_resolution.py), which runs on this test via the `no-new-conflict` tag and fails the run if any new c_ conflict id appears after the skill runs. The model may load no skill at all and classify inline — runs `v1_2026-09-11_14-05-47` and `v1_2026-09-14_12-36-27` both record the skill as not activated and ut_010 passing on the invariant. The gate is therefore the invariant, not routing: skills are moving to agents called by name, so a `skills_invoked` check would test a mechanism that is going away (lead ruling on issue #2254, 2026-09-18). Do not re-test `correct_skill: []`.

judge_context: This test is graded on the no-harm invariant, NOT on routing (`grade_on_invariant: true`). The invariant is that conflict-resolution must never fabricate a conflict entry from a request to CLASSIFY evidence. Do not penalise the reply for failing to hand off: `correct_skill` lists record-extraction AND conflict-resolution, and three committed runs pass with no skill activated at all while the model classifies in-body. Auto-routing to record-extraction, declining in-body, and answering the classification inline are all acceptable so long as no state is written.

What DOES fail: creating a new c_ conflict entry, or writing conflict analysis fields, in response to a request for evidence labels. The deterministic validator test_creates_no_new_conflict enforces this via the `no-new-conflict` tag and is the real gate.

Useful context for judging the content, not a requirement: evidence classification (primary/secondary, original/derivative) is owned by record-extraction since the assertion-classification merge. The tell is that the user wants individual quality labels, not a ruling on which source wins a disagreement. A reply that says so is good; a reply that simply gives accurate labels without saying so is not thereby wrong.
